official.deadline_note: There is no scholarship application deadline: the awards are automatic and follow admission, payment and transcript records. Rolling admission runs 1 October 2026 - 31 March 2027 and LUT warns that programmes may fill up before the final deadline. The early bird discount requires payment within 21 days of the official admission email, and the second-year award requires 60 ECTS on the Transcript of Records by 31 July.

official.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition fee for LUT's international master's programmes is EUR 15,000 per academic year. The Early bird discount of EUR 5,000 reduces the first academic year fee, leaving a remaining first-year fee of EUR 10,000, and the second-year LUT scholarship of EUR 5,000 leaves EUR 10,000 payable for the second academic year (EUR 15,000 without the scholarship). LUT states that tuition fee scholarships are a discount on the tuition fee and are not paid to the student.

official.description: LUT University reduces tuition for fee-paying students of its two-year master's programmes in two automatic steps: an Early bird discount of EUR 5,000 in the first academic year and a LUT scholarship of EUR 5,000 in the second academic year. Both awards are discounts on the tuition fee rather than money paid to the student, and neither covers living costs. There is no separate application or competitive selection.

official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic 6.5, New TOEFL iBT 4.5, TOEFL iBT 92, PTE Academic 68, Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency pass, or National Certificate of Language Proficiency (YKI) level 5 in all subtests; alternatively a higher education degree completed in English in an EU/EEA country, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Switzerland, the UK or the USA, or a degree completed in Finnish or Swedish in Finland. Results are valid for two years and must remain valid at least 15 days after the application is submitted, and are uploaded at application or within the personal seven-day supplementary deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you apply for: LUT automatically knocks EUR 5,000 off the first-year tuition of every fee-paying master's student who accepts the study place and pays the remaining EUR 10,000 within 21 days, then repeats the EUR 5,000 reduction in year two for anyone who banks 60 ECTS by 31 July. If both awards land you pay EUR 10,000 per academic year against a full fee of EUR 15,000, which is a tuition saving of EUR 10,000 across the degree. Nothing here touches living costs, housing, travel or the residence permit, so you must fund those yourself from the day you accept. Treat the two payment windows and the 31 July transcript deadline as hard cash deadlines rather than merit targets.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants to LUT's two-year English-taught master's programmes who can move EUR 10,000 quickly after an offer arrives
application_readiness_checklist: Have the EUR 10,000 first-year payment ready to transfer within 21 days of the admission email, and set up an international payment route before admission decisions arrive
Build a personal study plan that places at least 60 ECTS in the first academic year, since credits outside the plan and credits recognised from previous degrees never count
Check the transcript the moment it is published in August, because the credit check runs automatically with no application and no correction window afterwards
Make sure an accepted English test result stays valid for at least 15 days after you submit, and upload it at application or within the seven-day supplementary deadline
Apply as early as possible in the rolling round because programmes can fill before the 31 March 2027 final deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 21-day payment window, which is the only condition attached to the first-year discount
Credits not on the Transcript of Records by 31 July, including ECTS recognised from earlier degrees, which do not count toward the 60
Skipping core or specialisation studies to bank ECTS quickly and delaying graduation, which pushes study into a fifth semester where additional fees may be charged
Paying the second-year tuition fee late, which forfeits the second-year award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, housing, meals, travel to Finland and residence-permit costs, plus the EUR 10,000 tuition still payable in each academic year after the discount; LUT publishes no living-cost support for these awards
document_audit: Keep every official admission email as proof of the 21-day clock, because the early bird discount is stated on the admission letter itself
Your personal study plan and Transcript of Records are the only documents that decide the second-year award, so reconcile them course by course before 31 July
alerts: Rolling admission ends 31 March 2027, but LUT warns that programmes may fill earlier, so a late application can lose the study place entirely
The 21-day early bird window is short for international bank transfers, so start payment paperwork before the offer arrives

Terms change by intake year (intake 2025 or earlier received a EUR 6,000 second-year scholarship against a EUR 13,500 fee), so read the scholarship page for your own intake rather than older blog posts
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through rolling admission on LUT's application portal; there is no scholarship form - the discount is applied when you accept the place and pay, and the second-year award is confirmed from the transcript in August

official.deadline_note: The 2026 call closed on 31 August 2026 at 23:59 (EET) and no date for the next call has been published. Candidates who proceed to the selection stage must provide an accepted proof of English language skills by 31 December 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call (one annual call); employment starts between 1 January and 31 March 2027; no next-call date published yet
official.status_note: The University of Helsinki states the call closed on 31 August 2026 after 2,159 applications from 110 nationalities; 1,023 applicants (47%) passed the eligibility check and Excellence Evaluation by independent external evaluators started in September 2026, with written applications to be finalised by mid-October 2026 and interview rounds in late October 2026.
benefits: A competitive salary in accordance with MSCA COFUND principles, approximately EUR 2,900 gross per month with taxes deducted automatically
A family or special needs allowance may be paid where applicable
Support for relocation and integration into Finland and the University of Helsinki
Comprehensive occupational health care and staff benefits
Temporary secondments or research visits outside the University of Helsinki in RESDOC associated partner organisations when separately agreed
Training in AI, systems thinking and innovation, with expertise built in sustainable development, social responsibility, risk management and policy frameworks
eligibility: Hold a Master's degree or equivalent qualifying for doctoral studies, fully completed and dated in the certificate by the call deadline of 31 August 2026

Not hold a PhD degree, and be an early-stage researcher with less than 4 years of full-time-equivalent research experience after the Master's degree (research-related work such as university teaching, laboratory and field work, academic coordination and industry research positions counts)
Comply with the MSCA mobility rule: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Finland in the 36 months before the call deadline (1 September 2023 - 31 August 2026)
Not be permanently employed by the University of Helsinki, and be willing to reside in Finland for the full four-year duration
Fulfil the University of Helsinki's English language requirements; applications must be submitted in English
Propose a research topic fitting one of the four RESDOC themes with available supervision; the research may focus on any region of the world
requirements: Use the University of Helsinki's predefined templates for every required section - applications that do not follow the templates are disqualified at the eligibility stage
Respect the given font size and page limits, including in the Letter of Motivation
File names must use the Latin alphabet (A-Z) and Arabic numerals (0-9) only
Each PDF must not exceed the recommended maximum size of 5 MB
Do not include additional attachments - only the mandatory documents are evaluated
Report any use of AI tools in the motivation letter and research plan; fully AI-generated applications do not meet expectations
documents: Europass CV created in English, named CV_Lastname_Firstname (PDF, max 5 MB), with research experience and Finnish stays clearly dated
Letter of Motivation and doctoral study plan in the predefined template, named Motivation_Lastname_Firstname, uploaded in the 'Cover Letter' field
Research proposal, ethics self-assessment and intersectoral mobility plan in the predefined template, named Proposal_Lastname_Firstname, with 2-3 suggested supervisors
Scanned Master's degree certificate and transcript of records, with official stamped translations and the originals when not in Finnish, Swedish or English
Proof of English language skills - optional at application, but required by 31 December 2026 for candidates who proceed to the selection stage
selection_criteria: Written application scored 0-5 per criterion with a pass threshold of 3 and a weight of 70%
Interview scored 0-5 per criterion with a pass threshold of 3 and a weight of 30%

Written criteria: thematic fit with RESDOC themes, quality of the research plan (clarity, novelty, methodology, impact, ethics), feasibility including risks and mitigation, study and intersectoral mobility plan, and applicant competence
Interview criteria: ability to present the proposed project and answer questions, and academic and professional alignment with the available research options and supervision
Evaluations are conducted independently and solely on the published criteria; candidates must not contact evaluation panel members about their application
coverage: Gross salary of approximately EUR 2,900 per month, determined according to Horizon Europe MSCA COFUND principles, covering living costs in Finland
Relocation and integration support, plus a family or special needs allowance where applicable
Occupational health care and staff benefits as an employee of the University of Helsinki
Temporary secondments or research visits with RESDOC associated partner organisations when separately agreed
application_method: Apply only through the University of Helsinki online recruitment system, in English, by the call deadline
Attach the mandatory template documents: Europass CV, Letter of Motivation and doctoral study plan, and research proposal with ethics self-assessment and intersectoral mobility plan
Submit only one application; applicants may show interest in two of the four themes
official.application_route: One online application in English through the University of Helsinki recruitment system using the mandatory templates; no separate scholarship form
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction, but the MSCA mobility rule bars anyone who resided or carried out their main activity in Finland for more than 12 months between 1 September 2023 and 31 August 2026, and doctoral researchers must reside in Finland for the full four-year duration
official.international_eligibility: Open internationally: the 2026 call attracted applicants from 110 nationalities, with the largest numbers from India, Pakistan, Iran, Nigeria, Ethiopia and China; due to restricted system access, applicants residing in Iran had to contact the project office for submission instructions
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research topic must fit one of four interdisciplinary themes: Infectious Diseases and Antimicrobial Resistance in Changing Environment; Biodiversity and Nature's Resilience; Secure and Sustainable Food and Water Systems; and Just Socio-Ecological Transition
official.research_requirement: A doctoral research proposal in the predefined template including an ethics self-assessment and an intersectoral mobility plan, with 2-3 suggested supervisors, prepared independently so that the process stays free of preselection; any use of AI must be reported
official.duration: Four years, fixed-term full-time (100%) employment contract 2027-2030 including a six-month trial period; the main supervisor must come from the University of Helsinki, with co-supervision possible from other universities or research organisations
official.description: RESDOC (Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project) is an international doctoral training project at the University of Helsinki in Finland, co-funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions COFUND scheme (Grant Agreement No 101261796) and the University itself. It recruited 30 doctoral researchers in 2026 for four-year fixed-term full-time employment contracts starting between 1 January and 31 March 2027, at a competitive MSCA COFUND salary. Doctoral researchers conduct full-time research within four interdisciplinary themes and are enrolled in one of the University's 14 doctoral programmes; the project runs from 2027 to 2031.
official.program_type: Employment-based doctoral training positions (MSCA COFUND / Horizon Europe)
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English. Applicants must state, but not document, their English proficiency at the application phase; candidates who proceed to the selection stage must provide a valid proof of English language skills accepted by the University of Helsinki by 31 December 2026. The University accepts various ways of demonstrating English proficiency depending on the applicant's background, and no specific test scores are published on the RESDOC pages.

applicant_utility.summary: RESDOC hired 30 doctoral researchers as salaried University of Helsinki employees at roughly EUR 2,900 gross a month on four-year contracts, and the 2026 round drew 2,159 applications from 110 nationalities. More than half of those applicants, 1,136 people, were ruled ineligible or disqualified before any evaluation of research quality, mostly over templates, formats and missing documents. The 2026 call is now closed with external evaluation under way, and no next-call date has been announced, so treat this as an annual autumn competition where administrative compliance decides who is even read. The mobility rule and the dated final diploma requirement eliminate otherwise strong candidates in bulk.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers within four years of their Master's degree who have not lived in Finland recently and want an employment-based PhD in sustainability, biodiversity, food and water systems, infectious diseases or socio-ecological transition
application_readiness_checklist: Download the three mandatory templates and write into them without changing fonts, structure or page limits
Compress every attachment to under 5 MB and rename files as CV_, Motivation_, Proposal_ or Certificate_Lastname_Firstname using only Latin letters and Arabic numerals
In the Europass CV, list every post-Master's research engagement with dates and full-time-equivalent conversion, and every stay in Finland with months and exact dates
Secure a final Master's degree certificate and transcript before the deadline - an attestation of completion is explicitly not accepted - with official stamped translations where needed
Identify 2-3 potential supervisors from the RESDOC pool in advance and check your topic fits one of the four themes, while still writing the proposal yourself
common_rejection_risks: Missing or incomplete documents: 1,136 of 2,159 applicants failed at the eligibility stage, more than were rejected on quality
Using own templates, changing fonts, exceeding page limits or adding extra attachments that are not evaluated
Non-Latin file names or PDFs above the 5 MB limit
CV gaps in research experience or Finnish stays that make the early-stage researcher or mobility criteria impossible to assess
Submitting an attestation of completion instead of a final diploma certificate
Fully AI-written motivation letters or research plans, which the project states do not meet expectations and must declare AI use
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The first Finnish residence permit costs EUR 530 and a continuing permit EUR 230; the salary is taxed automatically so net income is below the EUR 2,900 gross figure, and relocation costs before the first salary are yours to fund even though the project offers relocation and integration support. No private health insurance is needed because the employment contract covers occupational health care.

alerts: The MSCA mobility rule disqualifies anyone with more than 12 months in Finland between 1 September 2023 and 31 August 2026 - write those stays out with exact dates in the CV so they can be verified
